name: Tuppenny Ha'penny Loo
description: Tuppenny Ha'penny Loo is a simple matching/penalty card game. Players hold 5 cards and 5 buttons. Cards are played face down in turn; if the next player matches the rank, the previous player pays buttons to the pot. Consecutive matches escalate the penalty (1, 2, 3 buttons). Player who runs out of buttons loses.

history.origins: Loo originated in England as a short form of Lanterlu (or Lanterloo), a 17th-century trick-taking game that may have reached Britain from France around the Restoration. The earliest known description dates from the 17th century; Loo appeared in most general English and American card game manuals through the end of the 19th century. In Britain it was later superseded by Nap and in America by Poker, though it survived as a parlor and family game. Tuppenny Ha'penny Loo is a simplified, low-stakes variant using rank matching and buttons instead of chips, suited to children and casual play.
timeline: 17th century: Earliest known description of Loo; game spread in English and American manuals through the 19th century.

rules.objective: Be the last player with buttons. Avoid matching the previous card's rank when playing, since matching forces the previous player to pay buttons into the pot; consecutive matches escalate (1, then 2, then 3 buttons).
rules.gameplay: Play cards face down in sequence. If next player matches rank of previous card: previous player pays 1 button. Second consecutive match: 2 buttons. Third: 3 buttons. Play all 5 cards per round. Player out of buttons loses.

strategy.basic: Play rare ranks to avoid matches.
strategy.intermediate: Track which ranks have been played.

scoring.description: Buttons as currency. Match = penalty to previous player.
